To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) an exact resonance condition is obtained for rigid symmetric second order bifurcating structure; (2) the resonance condition can reduced to two forms that facilitate volume estimate of bifurcations; (3) an experimental study to determine resonance modes of 7 glass structures was performed and the volume estimates were in close agreement with the actual volume.

an exact resonance condition for a symmetric second-order bifirating structure is presented, which can be reduced to two forms for volume estimation, and the experimental results indicate that both methods provide volume estimates with an error less than 5%.

the resonance modes of a symmetric second-order bifuring structure satisfy an exact resonance condition, and that the volume of a symmetric second-ordere bifurcating structure can be approximated by two methods: (1) the fundamental frequency method, and (2 the equivalent length method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new method of estimating volume of bifurcated structures from their resonance characteristics.
the development and application of a resonance mode analysis technique for volume estimation of symmetrically bifurcating vascular systems.
a method to estimate the volume of a bifurcating structure by measuring the resonant frequency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fundamental frequency method is more accurate than the equivalent-length method.
the resonance modes of a symmetric bifurcating structure can be used as a reliable method for volume estimation.
the resonance condition for symmetric second-order structures can be reduced into the form of a volume estimate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the volume estimation of a symmetric bifurcating structure can be achieved by either of two methods, which are both simple to apply and are accurate.
the fundamental frequency method is recommended for volume estimation of bifurlcating structures, whereas the equivalent-length method is recommended for structures with multiple bifurcations.
resonance mode analysis can be a useful method for estimating the volume of bifurcated structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple and effective method is now available to estimate the volume of branching structures, which is important in the study of vascular networks.
the fundamental frequency method can be easily implemented in a noninvasive manner for in situ measurement of volume of bifurcations in the human body.
a single resonance mode is sufficient for volume estimation of symmetric bifurcating systems.
